historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes reset risk but assumes bootdev none semantics, exposes credentials and neither reads back state nor defines the expected path or restores it.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires owner/vendor resolution of default-path and one-time semantics before any write or reboot.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: None should be tested as absence of a boot override, not as an unnamed device. Acceptance needs both negative evidence that no override remains and positive evidence that the recorded baseline default path was selected.

original_test_intent: Validate the platform-defined None/default boot setting and its one-time Enabled behavior by proving the approved SUT returns to the owner-defined normal boot path after a controlled reboot.
original_method: Record the actual baseline default boot device and order, resolve vendor None and Enabled semantics, verify no conflicting override, obtain approval, apply the protected one-time None/default setting, read it back, reboot once under POST/console observation, prove selection of the recorded default path, then verify the override is consumed and the original boot configuration and OS health remain intact.
manual_activity: The owner defines the normal boot path and approves the reboot; an operator observes POST/console device selection, stops unsafe paths and controls restoration and recovery.
required_inputs: Vendor definition of Boot settings None
Definition of Enabled and one-time versus persistent scope
Disposition of the PXE regression note for this None case
Maintenance window and final reboot approval
safety_requirements: Do not guess that IPMI bootdev none maps to the Web value
Use one-time scope only and never alter persistent order silently
Read back setting and persistence before reboot
Use protected credentials and exact target validation
Stop on wrong device, installer, PXE loop, boot failure or timeout
Clear any lingering override and restore baseline
Preserve logs and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate vendor mapping and owner-defined default path
Apply/read back one approved one-time setting after confirmation
Request and perform one approved reboot
Collect structured state while operator verifies POST/console path
Verify override consumption and restored health
engineer_actions: Define None/default path and Enabled semantics

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: chassis bootdev none may not represent the Web None value on this firmware; the literal command exposes credentials, resets immediately and lacks readback, POST evidence and cleanup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-mapped protected boot-control path, verify one-time None/default readback, then reboot once under independent observation and prove both default-path selection and override consumption.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: None, Enabled/Save, reboot and 10/20-minute estimates remain; specific path becomes the recorded owner-approved default rather than a guess.

modernized_recommendation.status: DEFAULT-PATH BOOT WITH NO ACTIVE OVERRIDE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a before/write/pre-reboot/post-boot state ledger showing baseline default order, transient None representation, actual POST-selected device and consumed override.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the otherwise unnamed path and separates no-override state from a boot-device token.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful reset or OS return does not prove the intended default device was selected or that a persistent override was avoided.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may encode None as clearing parameters, as NoOverride or as a vendor value; treating these as interchangeable without mapping can leave stale flags or choose a different boot path.

project_override_considerations: The Project must specify the expected default device/path and whether the PXE regression note applies to this None row or only the following PXE row. No PXE fixture is inferred for None unless explicitly retained.
expected_evidence: Approved target/window, baseline boot order/default device, resolved None/Enabled semantics and regression disposition
Protected boot-control write/readback showing exact one-time or cleared-override state
Reset plus POST/console/OS timeline proving the recorded default path
Post-boot readback proving override consumption and no persistent order change
Restored OS/BMC health and preserved audit/SEL/OS logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: None and specific path can be coherently implemented as clearing a one-time override and following the recorded default path. The PXE regression note is ambiguous supporting context that must be dispositioned, but it does not force a competing target in this row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: None semantics, default path and regression applicability are normal owner/vendor inputs; execution is gated until resolved but the workflow need not be invented.

review_improvement: Turns an undefined none-to-somewhere reset into a measurable proof that no override remains and the known default boot path is selected and restored safely.
independent_technical_reasoning: A boot-control value of None usually describes control state, not a destination. Therefore success requires correlating the absence or consumption of override flags with the independently recorded default order and the device actually selected during POST. Observing only the final OS can mask fallback through an unintended device.
